transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO - Azureling), Elena (Lead ML Eng), Jordan (Infra), Maya (Product)

[00:00] Alex: hey thanks everyone for joining, i'm alex from redwood inference, together with priya our solutions engineer. goal today is to understand your quickstart needs and any constraints around privacy or vpc connectivity.
[00:12] Samir: yeah thanks alex, quick note we're on pacific time here, so appreciated. main thing for us is we want to spin up a prototype for conversational search inside our authoring tool, ideally self-serve first, but i need to understand the path to private later.
[00:25] Elena: hi all, im elena. our primary constraints really are latency under 300ms p95 for short prompts, and we also have strict data retention rules — no logs stored outside our control.
[00:38] Priya: got it, Elena. just to clarify, when you say self-serve do you mean developer onboarding via hosted API with free credits and rapid TTFT, or do you expect a managed pilot with dedicated capacity?
[00:50] Samir: start hosted for speed, free credits likely okay for product team to mock up flows. but if results look good we need a path to vpc or private deployment within two months.
[01:02] Jordan: and from infra side we prefer VPC peering or a private link, cannot open broad internet egress from our prod subnets.
[01:12] Alex: totally reasonable — our typical flow is free credits to get to first token within hours for devs, then a pilot where we either set up Dedicated capacity or Redwood Private (VPC). for VPC we support peering and private connect and have an on-prem option if required.
[01:25] Maya: what's the actual TTFT for an engineer — like, how long until they can call the api and see a response?
[01:30] Priya: in practice if you use our quickstart sdk and the sandbox model, you can do your first request within 30–90 minutes, including auth and environment variables. If you want to route through your VPC the initial setup is more like a few days to a week depending on network approvals.
[01:45] Elena: okay, that matches expectations. the other question is about tokens and cost — we want guidance on what tokens per request look like for chat vs structured generations.
[01:54] Alex: we'll send a cost-per-token cheat sheet. for prototyping with a 2–3 turn chat, expect small cost, and credits cover initial usage. for production we often recommend quantization and model recommendations to hit cost targets.
[02:06] Samir: security is big — do you have SOC2, SOC2 type II? any iso or feeding our internal audit?
[02:12] Alex: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO is in progress — i'll attach the SOC2 excerpts and our security pack in the follow-up. we also provide audit logs, SSO via SAML/SCIM, and KMS integrations for Redwood Private.
[02:24] Jordan: does KMS work for hosted or only private? we need customer-managed keys ideally.
[02:29] Priya: customer-managed KMS is supported on Private and for Dedicated we can support Bring Your Own Key via KMS federation. hosted public api uses Redwood-managed encryption but we provide at-rest encryption and TLS in transit.
[02:43] Elena: any caveats on PII detection or automatic retention? we need guaranteed no PII retention for certain endpoints.
[02:49] Alex: for hosted quickstart you can opt out of data retention per account; for enterprise private/dedicated, logs are either disabled or kept under your control per the contract. we'll include a sample data-retention config.
[02:59] Samir: good. benchmark-wise, priya, can you speak to latency on your verified models? we will likely evaluate 8k vs 32k contexts — our docs ingestion uses long contexts sometimes.
[03:12] Priya: yes, for standard 8k models we've measured ~80–150ms per token on our hosted fleet for the small-to-medium LLMs with batching disabled, p95 depends on seq length. for 32k context models it rises, and we typically recommend enabling streaming responses and prefix/K V cache in the runtime to lower effective latency.
[03:30] Jordan: k v cash?
[03:33] Elena: K V cache — i think transcription had earlier said K V cash on another call, haha.
[03:36] Priya: yep kv cache — that's how we persist attention state between turns to avoid re-encoding the whole prompt, saves latency and tokens.
[03:44] Maya: would we need to change model architecture or anything? our devs want to keep the pipeline simple.
[03:49] Priya: no model change required. the runtime handles KV and batching. for cost you can choose quantized variants or smaller models automatically.
[03:57] Samir: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private here? we want isolation and consistent performance but also don't want to manage infra.
[04:05] Alex: Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved capacity — you get a GPU pool for your tenant with predictable throughput and an SLA. Private gives you a private control plane with VPC connectivity; you can have it in your cloud account or on-prem with our package if needed. Private tends to be chosen when customers need customer-managed KMS or strict network isolation.
[04:22] Jordan: for VPC peering we have a specific process — we need egress restrictions and cross account roles. is there a runbook?
[04:29] Priya: yes, we have a VPC runbook. it covers peering, private link, firewall rules, and typical CIDR allowances. i'll attach it. setup usually needs a ticket with your network team and a small config on our side.
[04:41] Elena: whats the expected time to get a bench that represents our production requests? we want to run perf & cost sims.
[04:48] Priya: if you provide a sample workload (typical prompt lengths, calls per second), we can run a targeted bench in 3–5 business days on our end, longer if you want private-dedicated hardware reservations.
[05:00] Samir: ok — sounds like next steps are a security package and a bench template. also we want to try hosted quickstart with a developer credit pool. how do credits apply to different endpoints?
[05:10] Alex: credits apply to token usage and embeddings; some higher-tier models may have a different multiplier but we will map that in the credits doc. they also provide access to the sandbox models for prototyping.
[05:20] Maya: any friction on SDK setup? our devs use node and python.
[05:24] Priya: we have official SDKs for node/python and examples for chat, streaming and embeddings. sample app with an express + react quickstart is in the repo — you can clone and hit first token within an hour if you have an API key.
[05:36] Jordan: what about rate limits and bursting? if we cold start with a PLG flow and suddenly hit 500 rps, what's the behavior?
[05:43] Alex: hosted accounts have quota & rate limits; we can present autoscaling policies for Dedicated. for PLG, we recommend a token-level cache and gradual rollout to avoid burst costs. if you need to handle spikes we'll propose a burst capacity plan in Dedicated.
[05:56] Samir: curious about model fallback — if a preferred model isn't available under load, can you route to a cheaper variant automatically?
[06:03] Priya: yes, smart routing policies can fall back based on cost/latency. you can pin endpoints to model versions and allow fallback to compatible quantized variants when capacity is low.
[06:15] Elena: great. can you also outline what the pilot metrics should be so our PM knows success criteria?
[06:21] Alex: typically we propose: p95 latency < target, cost per 1k tokens under target, answers passing our quality evals on a set of seed prompts, and stability (uptime) during test window. we'll share a template.
[06:33] Maya: timeline — if we start with credits this week, can we have a pilot by mid-august?
[06:38] Priya: yes mid-august is plausible. dev quickstart this week, bench next week, pilot kickoff late july/early august depending on approvals.
[06:47] Alex: ok let me recap quickly — Action items: alex send security & soc2 excerpts and credits doc; priya send bench template and vpc runbook + example benchmarks; jordan to share vpc diagram and egress constraints; samir/elena to send sample workload and latency/cost targets. we'll schedule the network deep-dive with our infra engineer next week. sound right?
[07:08] Samir: sounds right. thanks everyone.
[07:11] Elena: thanks.
[07:12] Maya: thanks!
